pages.title: Week 17: Kicking & Striking
pages.html:
Optima
Academy Online
Mission: Move!
3rd Grade PE · Unit 1.9 · Kicking & Striking
Week 17

Kicking & Striking: Power-Up Your Aim! ⚽

Whenever you kick a soccer ball, hit a balloon with your hand, or swing a bat — you're using kicking and striking skills. These are super important for sports... and also just super fun! Let's go.

1
Lesson 1
Kicking & Striking — What's the Difference?

Both are manipulative skills — using your body to move an object. But there's a key difference:

🦵
Kicking
You use your FOOT or LEG to move an object. Soccer = kicking!
🏏
Striking
You use your HAND or a TOOL (bat, paddle, racket) to hit an object.
2
Lesson 2
How to Kick Well
  1. 👀 Look at the ball and your target
  2. 🦶 Step next to the ball with your non-kicking foot
  3. 🦵 Swing your kicking leg back
  4. 💥 Connect with the middle or lower part of the ball using your shoelaces (not your toe!)
  5. ➡️ Follow through in the direction you want the ball to go
💡Did You Know?

The fastest soccer kick ever recorded was about 131 miles per hour — faster than most highway speed limits! Of course, you don't need to kick that hard. Control matters WAY more than speed. 🎯

3
Lesson 3
How to Strike Well
  1. 👀 Watch the object the whole time
  2. 🦶 Get in position — feet shoulder-width apart
  3. 💪 Pull back your hand or tool
  4. 💥 Swing through the object smoothly
  5. ➡️ Follow through in the direction you want it to go

Whether you're hitting a balloon with your hand or swinging a bat, the steps are basically the same!

🏃Activity Cue

Safe Strike Practice: Blow up a balloon. Tap it up in the air with your hand. How many times can you keep it from touching the floor? That's striking practice! 🎈

4
Lesson 4
Where You'll Use These Skills
⚽
Soccer
Kick the ball to teammates, kick it into the goal.
⚾
Baseball / T-ball
Strike the ball with a bat.
🎾
Tennis
Strike the ball with a racket.
🏐
Volleyball
Strike the ball with your hands and arms.
🌎Real-World Connection

The world's best soccer players miss kicks all the time — even Messi and Mbappé! What makes them great isn't NEVER missing — it's practicing MORE than everyone else. Every miss teaches them something. Same for you! 🌟

5
Lesson 5
Words to Know
  • Manipulative — Using your body or a tool to move an object.
  • Kick — Striking with your foot.
  • Strike — Hitting with your hand or a tool.
  • Coordination — Body parts working smoothly together.
  • Target — Where you're aiming.
  • Control — Moving an object exactly the way you want.
  • Follow-Through — Letting your motion finish AFTER you hit/kick.
📝Weekly Reflection

Quick reflection: What's your favorite thing to kick or strike? Have you ever scored a goal or hit a ball really well? How did it feel? 📝

→What's Next

Up next: Week 17 Discussion, then Week 18 — the Kicking & Striking Challenge!

pages.title: Teamwork & Cooperation
pages.html:
Optima

3rd Grade PE · Unit 1.10 · Teamwork & Cooperation
Unit 1.10

Teamwork: Stronger Together 🤝

A single ant can't carry a leaf very far — but a team of ants? They can move a leaf the size of a pizza! 🐜🍕 The same is true for YOU and your friends. When you work together, you can do amazing things.

1
Lesson 1
What's Teamwork?

Teamwork is when two or more people work TOGETHER to reach the same goal. In PE, teamwork looks like:

🏐
Passing
Sending the ball to a teammate so they can score.
⏳
Waiting Your Turn
Everyone gets a chance to play.
🩹
Helping Someone
If a friend falls, you help them up.
👏
Cheering On
"Nice job!" "You got this!" "Great try!"
2
Lesson 2
What's Cooperation?

Cooperation is HOW you show teamwork — through your actions and choices. Cooperating means:

  • 👂 Listening when others are talking
  • 📋 Following the rules and directions
  • 🔁 Taking turns during games
  • 🤝 Sharing equipment (balls, cones, mats)
  • 💬 Using kind words instead of yelling
  • 🧠 Helping solve problems together
💡Did You Know?

Even WOLVES use teamwork! When wolves hunt, they each have a job — some chase, some block, some sneak around. Without the whole team, none of them would catch dinner. Teamwork has been a superpower for millions of years. 🐺

3
Lesson 3
Teamwork in Action

Picture a soccer game. Can ONE player run the whole field, pass to themselves, defend the goal, AND score every point? 🤔

Nope! Soccer (and basketball, and volleyball, and dance teams) only work when EVERYONE plays their part.

That's why a winning team isn't always the team with the best player — it's the team that WORKS TOGETHER best. 🏆

4
Lesson 4
Why Teamwork Helps YOU
🧠
Brain Boost
You learn to listen, plan, and solve problems with others.
😄
More Friends
Being a good teammate makes people WANT to play with you.
💪
Faster Skills
When you practice with others, you learn way faster.
🎯
Confidence
Helping your team feels AWESOME.
🌎Real-World Connection

Think about your favorite video game with friends. The best players aren't always the ones who score the most — they're the ones who SHARE health potions, REVIVE teammates, and PLAN strategies together. That's teamwork! 🎮

5
Lesson 5
Words to Know
  • Teamwork — People working together for a shared goal.
  • Cooperation — Choosing actions that help your team.
  • Communication — Talking and listening with your team.
  • Encourage — Cheering on a teammate.
  • Respect — Caring about other people's feelings and ideas.
📝Weekly Reflection

Reflect: Think about a time you worked with a team (in PE, a game, a project, anywhere). What was YOUR job? Did you feel proud? 📝

→What's Next

Coming up: Teamwork Discussion with classmates, then your "Teamwork & Cooperation in Action!" assignment.

Unit 1.11

Sportsmanship & Respect: Be the Hero, Not the Villain 🦸

Anyone can win a game and act cool. The REAL superheroes? They're the kids who play fair, cheer on their friends, and stay kind — even when they lose. That's sportsmanship.

1
Lesson 1
What's Sportsmanship?

Sportsmanship is how you ACT during games and activities. Good sportsmanship means:

  • 🤝 Playing fair
  • 📜 Following the rules
  • 💛 Being kind to everyone — your teammates AND the other team
  • 🏆 Acting cool whether you win OR lose
2
Lesson 2
What's Respect?

Respect means treating people, rules, and equipment with care. It looks like:

👂
Listening
Paying attention when your teacher talks.
🏐
Caring for Stuff
Not throwing equipment or breaking things.
↔️
Personal Space
Not crowding or pushing classmates.
💬
Kind Words
No mean comments — even if you're frustrated.
💡Did You Know?

The Olympics has an award called the Pierre de Coubertin Medal — and it's the most respected award in the WHOLE Olympics. It doesn't go to the fastest runner or the strongest weightlifter. It goes to the athlete who shows the BEST sportsmanship. That's how much it matters! 🥇

3
Lesson 3
Good Sportsmanship in Action

What does a good sport look like?

  • 🤝 Saying "good game" after playing
  • 🙌 Helping someone up if they fall
  • 😊 Smiling when someone scores (even if it's not your team)
  • 📜 Following the rules even when no one is watching
  • 🧘 Staying calm if you lose
  • 🎉 Celebrating with your team if you win — but not making the other team feel bad
🏃Activity Cue

Think About It: Imagine you LOSE a game by ONE point. What would you say to the other team? What would you say to your own team? Practice in your head — those are the words you'll use next time! 💭

4
Lesson 4
Why It Matters

Good sportsmanship doesn't just make YOU look good — it makes EVERYONE'S day better.

🛡️
Safer Games
When everyone follows the rules, nobody gets hurt.
😄
More Friends
People want to play with kind kids.
💪
Better at Sports
When you respect coaches and teammates, you LEARN more.
😎
You Feel Awesome
Being a good sport makes YOU feel good inside.
🌎Real-World Connection

You know what? Sportsmanship isn't just for PE. It works EVERYWHERE — at school, with siblings, in video games, even when you're playing a board game with your family. The same skills make you a great teammate in life. 🌟

5
Lesson 5
Words to Know
  • Sportsmanship — How you act during games and activities.
  • Respect — Treating people, rules, and equipment with care.
  • Fair Play — Following the rules and being honest.
  • Encourage — To cheer someone on.
  • Self-Control — Staying calm and making good choices.
📝Weekly Reflection

Reflect: Tell me about a time you saw GREAT sportsmanship. What did the person do? How did it make YOU feel? 📝

→What's Next

Up next: Sportsmanship Discussion, then your Sportsmanship Reflection assignment!

3rd Grade PE · Unit 1.12 · Fitness Components
Unit 1.12

The 5 Fitness Components: Your Body's Superpower Squad 🦸‍♀️🦸‍♂️

"Being fit" isn't just one thing — it's actually FIVE different superpowers working together. Each one helps your body in a different way. Let's meet the Fitness Five!

1
Power #1
Cardiorespiratory Endurance ❤️

Cardiorespiratory endurance (that's a mouthful!) means how well your heart and lungs work together when you move for a long time. You use this when you:

  • 🏃 Run, jog, or chase friends
  • 🚴 Ride a bike
  • 🪢 Jump rope
  • 🏊 Swim

Strong heart and lungs = you can play LONGER without getting tired.

2
Power #2
Muscular Strength 💪

Muscular strength is how much power your muscles can produce. You use it when you:

  • 🎒 Carry a heavy backpack
  • 🚪 Open a heavy door
  • 🪜 Climb the monkey bars
  • 🪵 Hold a plank position

Strong muscles help you move safely and protect your body.

3
Power #3
Muscular Endurance 🔁

Muscular endurance is how LONG your muscles can keep working without giving up. (Different from strength — strength is power, endurance is stamina!) You use it when you:

  • 🤾 Do lots of jumping jacks in a row
  • 🪑 Hold a wall sit
  • 🚴 Keep pedaling up a hill
💡Did You Know?

Strength and endurance sound the same but they're different superpowers! Strength = lifting a heavy box ONCE. Endurance = lifting a lighter box 20 times in a row. Your body needs BOTH! 💪🔁

4
Power #4
Flexibility 🤸

Flexibility is how easily your body can stretch and bend. You use it when you:

  • 👟 Reach down to tie your shoes
  • 🙆 Stretch your arms way overhead
  • 🌀 Twist your body

Flexible bodies move more smoothly and don't get hurt as easily!

5
Power #5
Body Composition ⚖️

Body composition is just a fancy way of saying your body has a healthy MIX of muscles, bones, water, and fat. You don't need to count or measure — you just need to:

  • 🏃 Move your body every day
  • 🥗 Eat foods from all the food groups
  • 💧 Drink water
  • 😴 Get enough sleep

Your body is unique and amazing exactly how it is. The goal is to keep it strong and healthy. 💛

🌎Real-World Connection

Real athletes work on ALL 5 components — not just one. A soccer player needs endurance (running the whole game), strength (kicking hard), flexibility (stretching to reach the ball), AND a healthy body. That's why pros cross-train! 🏋️

6
Lesson 6
Words to Know
  • Cardiorespiratory Endurance — Heart & lung stamina.
  • Muscular Strength — How much power your muscles produce.
  • Muscular Endurance — How long muscles can keep working.
  • Flexibility — How well your body bends and stretches.
  • Body Composition — A healthy mix of muscles, bones, water, and fat.
📝Weekly Reflection

Reflect: Which of the 5 fitness components do you think YOU are strongest in? Which one would you like to get better at? 📝

→What's Next

Next stop: Fitness Components Discussion with classmates, then your reflection assignment.

3rd Grade PE · Unit 1.13 · Personal Space & Movement Safety
Unit 1.13

Personal Space & Safety: Be a Smart Mover 🦺

PE class is WAY more fun when nobody gets hurt — and that starts with knowing about personal space and safe movement. Let's learn the rules so we can all play hard AND stay safe.

1
Lesson 1
What's Personal Space?

Personal space is the invisible bubble around your body. 🫧 Everyone has one! Inside your bubble = YOU. Outside your bubble = everyone else.

An easy way to check your personal space:

The Airplane Test ✈️

Stretch your arms out to the sides like airplane wings. Spin slowly in a circle.

If you DON'T touch anyone or anything — perfect personal space! 🎉

If you DO touch something — move to a more open spot.

2
Lesson 2
Why Personal Space Matters
  • 🛡️ Helps you avoid bumping into others
  • 😌 Helps everyone feel comfortable
  • 🏃 Lets you move freely without accidents
  • 🤝 Shows respect for your classmates
🏃Activity Cue

Try this: Right now, do the airplane test in your room. Can you spin in a full circle without bumping anything? If not, move to a safer spot! 🎯

3
Lesson 3
What's Movement Safety?

Movement safety means moving your body in a way that keeps you AND your classmates safe. The big rules:

👂
Listen to the Teacher
Stop, start, or change activities when they say.
📋
Follow the Rules
Rules are there to keep games safe and fun.
🏐
Use Equipment Right
Balls are for playing — not throwing at people!
👀
Watch Where You're Going
Eyes UP, looking around, all the time.
4
Lesson 4
Safe Moves vs. Unsafe Moves

✅ Safe Movement Looks Like:

  • Walking when the teacher says walk
  • Freezing when the whistle blows
  • Holding equipment correctly
  • Looking around before you start moving

❌ Unsafe Movement Looks Like:

  • Running when you're told to stop
  • Throwing equipment at people
  • Pushing or tripping classmates
  • Not paying attention to what's happening
💡Did You Know?

Did you know your peripheral vision (the stuff you can see out of the SIDES of your eyes without turning your head 👀) is super important for staying safe? It helps you notice friends nearby — even when you're focused on a ball. Train it by trying to spot things on the edges of your view!

🌎Real-World Connection

Even pro athletes get hurt sometimes — but they get hurt WAY less because they practice safe movement. They warm up, they watch their surroundings, and they follow the rules. Smart movers stay in the game longer. 🏆

5
Lesson 5
Safety Rules to Remember
  1. 🛑 Stop, Look, and Listen before you move
  2. 🙌 Keep hands and feet to yourself
  3. 💬 Use kind words and calm actions
  4. ❓ Ask for help if you're not sure
  5. ✈️ Check your personal space often
6
Lesson 6
Words to Know
  • Personal Space — The bubble around your body.
  • Safety — Doing things in a way that prevents injuries.
  • Awareness — Knowing what's happening around you.
  • Equipment — The balls, cones, ropes, and gear we use.
  • Responsibility — Taking care of yourself AND others.
📝Weekly Reflection

Reflect: Was there ever a time you had to move out of someone's personal space? How did you handle it? What's ONE safety rule you want to remember? 📝

→What's Next

Up next: Personal Space Discussion, then your Personal Space & Movement Reflection!

pages.html:
Optima

3rd Grade PE · Unit 1.14 · Rhythmic Movement & Dance
Unit 1.14

Rhythm & Dance: Find Your Beat! 🎵

Your body is basically a musical instrument — it can dance, clap, stomp, and sway. Today we explore how moving to a BEAT can make you stronger, smarter, and WAY happier. Let's groove!

1
Lesson 1
What's Rhythm?

Rhythm is the pattern of beats you hear in music or sounds. It's like the heartbeat of a song! 💓

You can show rhythm by:

👏
Clapping
Snap your hands to the beat.
🦶
Stepping
March in place to the beat.
🦘
Jumping
Hop to every beat.
🌀
Swaying
Sway side to side smoothly.

Fast beats = move quickly! Slow beats = move slowly. Your body matches the music.

2
Lesson 2
What's Dance?

Dance is rhythmic movement where you use your whole body to express yourself with music. The amazing part? In PE class, there's NO right or wrong way to dance.

You can:

  • 💃 Move your arms, legs, and hips
  • 🎭 Show feelings and ideas through movement
  • 🤸 Mix big moves and small moves
  • 👯 Dance alone or with friends

What matters is that you try, move safely, and HAVE FUN. 🎉

💡Did You Know?

Dancing is actually GREAT for your brain! Studies show that people who dance regularly have sharper memories and better balance, even when they get old. Every time you learn a dance move, you're making your brain stronger. 🧠💃

3
Lesson 3
Why Dance is a Superpower
⚖️
Balance
Dance moves train you to stay steady.
🤝
Coordination
Body parts work together smoothly.
💪
Strength
Dance is a real workout!
⏱️
Timing
Your brain learns to match the beat.
🎨
Creativity
You invent moves nobody has done before!
😄
Confidence
Moving with music makes you feel awesome.
4
Try It
Rhythmic Movements You Can Try
  • 👏 Clapping games — Match the beat with hands
  • 📏 Line dances — Move together in steps
  • 🥶 Freeze dance — Move while music plays, freeze when it stops!
  • 🎨 Creative movement — Make up your OWN moves
  • 🌍 Cultural dances — Learn dances from around the world
🏃Activity Cue

Right now: Stand up. Put on your favorite song (or just clap a beat). Move your body for 30 seconds — any way you want! There's no wrong way. 🎵

🌎Real-World Connection

Even pro athletes use rhythm! Boxers train with music to learn timing. Soccer players have dribbling rhythms. Basketball players bounce balls to a beat. Rhythm is EVERYWHERE in sports — not just dance. 🥊⚽🏀

5
Lesson 5
Words to Know
  • Rhythm — The pattern of beats in music.
  • Beat — A single pulse in music (like a heartbeat).
  • Dance — Moving your body to music.
  • Tempo — How fast or slow the beat is.
  • Coordination — Body parts working together.
  • Expression — Showing feelings through movement.
📝Weekly Reflection

Reflect: What's your favorite song to move to? Have you ever made up your own dance move? Describe it! 📝

→What's Next

Coming up: Rhythmic Movement Discussion, then your Dance Reflection assignment!

pages.html:
Optima
Academy Online

3rd Grade PE · Unit 1.15 · Balance & Coordination
Unit 1.15

Balance & Coordination: Body Brain Magic ✨

Ever wonder how circus performers walk on tightropes? Or how athletes catch a ball while running full speed? It's balance and coordination — and YOU have these superpowers too. Let's level them up!

1
Lesson 1
What's Balance?

Balance is the ability to stay steady — not tipping over while standing, walking, or moving. You use balance ALL the time without thinking about it!

You use balance when you:

  • 🦩 Stand on one foot
  • 🛹 Ride a skateboard, bike, or scooter
  • 📏 Walk along a curb or beam
  • 🛑 Stop quickly while running
  • 🧘 Hold a yoga pose
2
Lesson 2
What's Coordination?

Coordination is when your eyes, hands, feet, and brain ALL work together smoothly. It's body teamwork inside YOU!

You use coordination when you:

  • 🏐 Catch a ball
  • 🏀 Dribble while running
  • 🦘 Jump rope
  • 👯 Learn dance moves
  • 👟 Tie your shoes
💡Did You Know?

Your brain has a special part called the cerebellum (sara-BELL-um) that controls balance and coordination. It's only the size of a peach 🍑 but it sends thousands of signals every second telling your muscles exactly what to do! 🧠⚡

3
Lesson 3
Why These Skills Matter
🛡️
Safer Moves
You're less likely to fall or trip.
🚀
Learn Faster
New skills come quicker.
🏆
Better at Sports
Every sport needs balance and coordination.
😎
More Confident
You feel in control of your body.
4
Try It
Balance & Coordination Games
  • 🦩 Flamingo stand — Stand on one foot for 30 seconds. Switch!
  • 📏 Tightrope walk — Walk along a line, one foot in front of the other
  • 🤸 Hopscotch — Mix hopping and jumping
  • 🎯 Throw & catch — Toss a ball, clap, then catch it
  • 🧘 Tree pose — Yoga balance pose
🏃Activity Cue

Quick test: Stand on ONE foot right now. Count how many seconds you can hold it before wobbling. Now try the OTHER foot. Are they different? Most people have one "better" foot! 🦩

🌎Real-World Connection

Surfers, skateboarders, gymnasts, ballet dancers — they ALL train balance and coordination every day. Even astronauts practice balance before going to space, because no gravity means no balance! 🚀

5
Lesson 5
Words to Know
  • Balance — Staying steady without falling.
  • Coordination — Body parts working together smoothly.
  • Posture — How you hold your body.
  • Stability — Being steady and in control.
  • Reaction Time — How fast your body responds.
📝Weekly Reflection

Reflect: What activity at home or recess needs the MOST balance for you? What part of coordination is trickiest? 📝

→What's Next

Up next: Balance & Coordination Discussion, then your reflection assignment.

pages.title: Goal Setting & Personal Fitness Plans
pages.html:
Optima
Academy Online
Mission: Move!
3rd Grade PE · Unit 1.16 · Goal Setting & Personal Fitness Plans
Unit 1.16

Goal Setting: Aim for Awesome 🎯

A goal is something you WANT to get better at. When you set a goal in PE, you're telling your body and brain, "Hey — I'm gonna work on this!" Goals turn dreams into action.

1
Lesson 1
What's a Goal?

A goal is something you want to improve, learn, or accomplish. In PE, fitness goals can be:

🏃
Endurance Goals
"I want to run for 5 minutes without stopping."
💪
Strength Goals
"I want to do 10 push-ups in a row."
🦩
Balance Goals
"I want to balance on one foot for 1 minute."
🤸
Flexibility Goals
"I want to touch my toes without bending my knees."
2
Lesson 2
What Makes a GOOD Goal?

Good goals share three things. Remember the word CSD — Clear, Safe, Doable!

  1. 🎯 Clear — You know exactly what you want to improve
  2. 🛡️ Safe — It won't hurt your body
  3. ✅ Doable — You can practice it often

Example of a great goal:

"I want to jump rope for 30 seconds without stopping by the end of the month."

It's CLEAR (jump rope for 30 seconds), SAFE (no injuries), and DOABLE (you can practice every day). 🎉

💡Did You Know?

People who WRITE DOWN their goals are 42% more likely to achieve them! That's why champions keep notebooks. ✍️ When you write a goal, your brain takes it seriously.

3
Lesson 3
What's a Personal Fitness Plan?

A personal fitness plan is your roadmap to reach your goal. It answers four big questions:

  1. 🎯 What is my goal?
  2. 🏃 What activity will I practice?
  3. 📅 How often will I practice?
  4. 👥 Who can help me?

Example Plan:

  • My Goal: Run longer without stopping
  • My Activity: Jogging around the block
  • How Often: 3 days a week
  • Helper: My mom or my older brother
4
Lesson 4
Why Set Goals?
🎯
You Stay Focused
You know what to practice.
🚀
You Get Motivated
Working toward something feels great.
📈
You See Progress
You can watch yourself improve!
😊
You Feel Proud
Reaching a goal = SO much confidence.
🏃Activity Cue

Try this: Right now, think of ONE thing you'd like to get better at — running farther, jumping higher, balancing longer, ANYTHING. Now make it CLEAR, SAFE, and DOABLE. That's your first goal! 🎯

🌎Real-World Connection

Every Olympic athlete, every NBA superstar, every dancer in a famous show — they ALL set goals. Big goals get broken into small goals. Small goals turn into wins. Wins turn into champions. You're already on the path! 🏆

5
Lesson 5
Words to Know
  • Goal — Something you want to get better at.
  • Fitness Plan — Your roadmap to reach a goal.
  • Progress — Slowly getting better over time.
  • Motivation — The reason you keep trying.
  • Achievement — When you accomplish your goal!
📝Weekly Reflection

Reflect: What's a PE goal you'd be proud to reach by the end of this course? Why does it matter to you? 📝

→What's Next

Up next: Goals & Plans Discussion, then your "My Fitness Goal & Plan" assignment — where you'll design your very own plan!

assignments.html:
Optima

3rd Grade PE · Unit 1.9 · Kicking & Striking
Unit 1.9

Flight Club Challenge: Cool Down Combo 🦉

🚀 Flight Club Challenge

Wrap up your kicking & striking unit with a chill-out combo. Three stretches to keep your body bendy and happy. 🌈

1
Flamingo Stretch (Quadriceps)

How to do it:

  • Stand tall and bend one knee, bringing your foot behind you.
  • Hold your ankle with your hand and keep your balance.
  • Keep your knees close together and hold for 10 seconds.
  • Switch legs and repeat.
  • Optional: Extend one arm forward like a flamingo's neck! 🦩

Benefits: Stretches the front of the thigh (quadriceps) and improves balance.

2
Forearm Plank

How to do it:

  • Get into a plank position with forearms on the ground and back flat.
  • Hold for 30 seconds without dropping your belly.
  • Challenge: Try tapping one shoulder at a time while holding the plank.
  • Modification: Try a knee plank if needed.

Benefits: Builds core and upper body strength.

3
Toe Touch Stretch (Waterfall)

How to do it:

  • Stand up tall with feet together.
  • Slowly bend forward and reach for your toes, keeping legs straight.

assignments.html:

Unit 1.10

Flight Club: Card Challenge 🃏

🚀 Flight Club Challenge

Game time! Use a deck of cards to power your workout. Every card = a different exercise. Are you ready, card sharks? 🎴

1
Setup
Materials You Need
  • 🎴 Option 1: A real deck of playing cards
  • 💻 Option 2: Internet access + the Calculator Soup Random Card Generator
2
How to Play
Step by Step
1
Draw a Card

Real deck: shuffle and draw one card at a time.

Online: click DRAW to see your card.

2
Match the Card to the Exercise

The SUIT tells you the exercise. The NUMBER tells you how many reps.

  • ♥️ Hearts = Jumping Jacks (8♥ = 8 jumping jacks)
  • ♠️ Spades = Push-Ups (K♠ = 13 push-ups)
  • ♦️ Diamonds = Sit-Ups / Crunches (4♦ = 4 sit-ups)
  • ♣️ Clubs = Squats (J♣ = 11 squats)

Face card values: Ace = 14, King = 13, Queen = 12, Jack = 11. Number cards = their number.

3
Pick Your Level
  • 🌱 Beginner — Draw 10 cards
  • ⭐ Intermediate — Draw 15 cards
  • 🚀 Advanced — Draw 20 cards

Complete the exercise BEFORE drawing another card!

🏃Activity Cue

Submit a video OR a guardian's statement saying you completed it!

✅Flight Crew Check-In

Flight Crew, check in!

  • Which suit did you draw the most?
  • Which exercise turned out to be your favorite?

Unit 1.11

Flight Club: Dice Challenge 🎲

🚀 Flight Club Challenge

Roll the dice, take your chances! Every number gets a different exercise. How will your workout go? Only fate knows! 🎲

1
Setup
Materials You Need
  • 🎲 One die (real or virtual)
  • 💻 Online option: Calculator Soup Dice Roller
  • 📏 Comfortable space to move
  • ⏱️ Timer or clock
2
How to Play
Step by Step
1
Roll the Die

Roll once. Look at your number.

2
Match Number to Exercise
  • 🎲 1 = Jumping Jacks — 10 reps
  • 🎲 2 = Push-Ups — 5 reps
  • 🎲 3 = Squats — 5 reps
  • 🎲 4 = Sit-Ups or Crunches — 10 reps
  • 🎲 5 = High Knees — 10 seconds
  • 🎲 6 = Mountain Climbers — 10 reps
3
Complete the Exercise

Do the exercise, then roll AGAIN for your next movement.

4
Repeat 10–12 Times

That's about a 10-minute full workout. 🔥

🏃Activity Cue

Optional Challenge Rounds:

  • 🆙 Level Up — Add 5 reps each round, or do all 6 exercises ONCE for a "Full Dice Circuit"
  • 👯 Partner Mode — Take turns rolling; each person does what the other rolls
  • ❤️ Cardio Boost — Add a 30-second jog in place between rolls
💭Think About It

Reflect:

  • Which exercise challenged you the most, and why?
  • How did your energy level change as you went?
  • How does this type of activity support YOUR fitness goals?
✅Flight Crew Check-In

Flight Crew, check in!

  • What number came up the most?
  • Did you push past your comfort zone?

Flight Club: Wall Touch Challenge 🧱

🚀 Flight Club Challenge

Touch every wall, fly through the cycles, master your balance and personal space. Let's GO! 🏃

1
Goal
What You're Doing

Move SAFELY to touch 3 or 4 different walls while practicing balance, coordination, and safe movement.

You can do this challenge by yourself OR with a guardian or friend!

2
How to Play
Set Up & Run It
1
Pick Your Walls

Choose 3 or 4 different walls in your space (gym, classroom, or home).

2
Start at Center

Begin at a center spot or safe starting area.

3
Touch Each Wall

When ready, move to touch each wall ONE at a time. Touch with your HAND, then return to the center before going to the next wall.

4
Complete Your Cycles

1 cycle = touching ALL walls. Pick your level:

  • 🌱 Beginner — 5 cycles
  • ⭐ Intermediate — 10 cycles
  • 🚀 Expert — 15 cycles
🏃Activity Cue

Submit a video OR a guardian's note saying you completed it!
